process_area.title: Process Mining, Process Analysis & Improvement Project Execution

value_stream.name: Operational Excellence, Process Mining & Continuous Improvement Program

fields.Participants: Process participants (frontline), process owner, OpEx CoE
fields.Trigger: New improvement project; unmapped process; annual architecture refresh
fields.Volume: Per targeted end-to-end process (e.g., P2P, O2C, store-replenishment, returns)

Automation Opportunity: - Process-map generation seeded by event-log discovery (W4058) to short-cut manual discovery
Controls: - CTL-630 (ensure controlled execution — Process Mining, Process Analysis & Improvement Project Execution (PA-133.2).)
- CTL-630: as-is map validated by process owner before analysis
Pain Points / Risks: - **Myth-vs-reality risk**: Documented process differs from actual; mitigated by gemba observation and process mining triangulation (W4058)
- **Scope-creep risk**: Mapping expands beyond the problem; mitigated by SIPOC and project charter
System Touchpoints: - Process repository (links to W4050); process mining prep (W4058); KPI baseline (W4054)

steps.activity: OpEx conduct process discovery: interviews, observation (gemba walk at store/DC), and document the as-is end-to-end flow with handoffs, systems, cycle times, and pain points
OpEx author the SIPOC and current-state value-stream map (process, flow, inventory, info, time) against the architecture (W4050)
OpEx validate the map with participants and the owner, and baseline against KPIs (W4054)

fields.Frequency: Per project + continuous monitoring for key processes
fields.Owner: OpEx Data Lead / BI (links to VS-28)
fields.Participants: OpEx CoE, BI/Data Engineering (links to VS-28.2), IT (links to VS-27), process owners
fields.Trigger: Improvement project; performance anomaly; periodic health check
fields.Volume: High-volume processes: POS (2.8M txn/mo links to VS-08), P2P (~9,500 invoices/mo links to VS-15), store replenishment (~5,000/mo links to VS-02), returns (links to VS-32), ecommerce orders (~42,900/mo links to VS-10)

workflows.name: Process Mining & Task Mining from ERP/System Event Logs

Automation Opportunity: - Continuous process-mining health monitoring with anomaly alerting; auto-identification of automation candidates
Controls: - CTL-630 (ensure controlled execution — Process Mining, Process Analysis & Improvement Project Execution (PA-133.2).)
- CTL-630: task-mining scoped with HR/Labor Relations; aggregated/role-level reporting; data minimization
Cross-references: - links to VS-28.2 (data eng), VS-84 (labor relations), VS-21 (compliance deviations), VS-30.2 (RPA)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Garbage-in risk**: Incomplete/dirty event logs distort the picture; mitigated by data-quality governance (links to VS-28.2)
- **Surveillance risk**: Task mining perceived as employee monitoring; mitigated by clear purpose, aggregation, and HR/Labor-Relations alignment (links to VS-84)
System Touchpoints: - Process-mining/task-mining platform; ERP/POS/WMS event logs (links to VS-08/VS-15/VS-10/VS-04); BI (links to VS-28.2); audit deviation feed (links to VS-21)
Time Estimate: - 2–6 weeks per major process to stand up; continuous thereafter

steps.activity: OpEx/BI ingest event logs from ERP/POS/WMS/ecommerce and run process mining to discover the *actual* process (variants, frequencies, deviations from standard) and task mining for desktop-based work
OpEx quantify process friction: throughput, bottlenecks, rework loops, wait times, automation candidates, and compliance deviations (e.g., bypassed approvals)
OpEx publish the mined view, reconcile with the as-is map (W4057), and feed findings to the pipeline (W4052) and continuous monitoring dashboard (W4066)

fields.Participants: Process participants, subject-matter experts, process owner

Automation Opportunity: - Bottleneck auto-detection from event logs; root-cause hypothesis templating
Controls: - CTL-630 (ensure controlled execution — Process Mining, Process Analysis & Improvement Project Execution (PA-133.2).)
- CTL-630: RCA validated with data; findings peer-reviewed by Master Black Belt
Cross-references: - links to W4058 (mining), W4060 (re-design), W4065 (benefit case)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Symptom-vs-cause risk**: Treating symptoms; mitigated by structured RCA and data validation
- **Assumption risk**: Conclusions without data; mitigated by mining/KPI evidence
System Touchpoints: - Process-mining data (W4058); KPI baseline (W4054); analytics (links to VS-28)

steps.activity: OpEx identify constraints/bottlenecks (theory-of-constraints) and quantify their impact on end-to-end cycle time and throughput
OpEx facilitate root-cause analysis (5-Why, fishbone, Pareto) on defects/rework/wait, validating with data from mining (W4058)
OpEx document findings, the future-state hypothesis, and feed into re-design (W4060) and the business case (W4065)

fields.Participants: Process participants, process owner, Quality (links to VS-31), OCM (links to VS-134)

workflows.name: Process Re-Design, Standard Work & SOP Authoring

Automation Opportunity: - SOP generation from process design; digital SOPs with in-line controls; change cascade to LMS
Controls: - CTL-630 (ensure controlled execution — Process Mining, Process Analysis & Improvement Project Execution (PA-133.2).)
- CTL-630: SOP version control and approval (links to VS-30.3); new control points registered
Cross-references: - links to VS-30.3 (SOP library), VS-31 (quality), VS-134 (OCM), W4063 (controls)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Over-engineering risk**: Future-state too complex to sustain; mitigated by standard-work discipline and pilot validation
- **Doc-reality drift risk**: SOPs not followed; mitigated by OCM (W4064) and compliance monitoring (W4092)
System Touchpoints: - SOP/document library (links to VS-30.3); quality system (links to VS-31); training/LMS (links to VS-19.4); control register (links to internal-controls-matrix)

steps.activity: OpEx design the future-state process (eliminate waste, re-sequence, re-allocate, digitize/automate candidates per W4062) and standard work (the best-known method)
OpEx/Quality author/update SOPs, job aids, and training content, integrate with the SOP digital library (links to VS-30.3), and define the new control points (W4063)
OpEx validate the design with a pilot (W4061), confirm KPI improvement vs baseline (W4054), and prepare for rollout (W4064)

fields.Participants: Pilot site leadership, participants, BI (links to VS-28), process owner
fields.Volume: Per improvement project (often a single store/DC/category pilot)

workflows.name: Improvement Pilot Design, Execution & Hypothesis Testing

Automation Opportunity: - Automated A/B-style pilot measurement with significance testing
Controls: - CTL-630 (ensure controlled execution — Process Mining, Process Analysis & Improvement Project Execution (PA-133.2).)
- CTL-630: go/no-go decision recorded with evidence; rollback plan pre-approved
Pain Points / Risks: - **False-positive risk**: Pilot succeeds due to Hawthorne effect, not the change; mitigated by control sites and sufficient duration
- **Scale-up risk**: Pilot works locally but not at scale; mitigated by representative pilot sites and rollout phasing (W4064)
System Touchpoints: - KPI monitoring (W4054/VS-28); pilot-site ERP/POS config; analytics (links to VS-28)

steps.activity: OpEx design the pilot: hypothesis, scope (store/DC/category), duration, success metrics vs baseline (W4054), control/compare plan, and rollback plan
OpEx/leadership execute the pilot at the site, monitor daily, capture issues, and adjust within the pilot window
OpEx/BI evaluate results (statistical significance where volume allows), decide go/no-go/adjust for rollout (W4064), and document lessons (W4071)

fields.Owner: OpEx Process Lead / Automation CoE (links to VS-30.2)
fields.Participants: OpEx CoE, Automation CoE (VS-30.2), Enterprise Architecture (VS-113), IT (VS-27), Finance (VS-17.4)
fields.Trigger: Mining/analysis identifies manual/repetitive work; automation candidate
fields.Volume: Enterprise automation pipeline (RPA, IDP, workflow, integration)

Automation Opportunity: - Opportunity scoring; automation-portfolio analytics (realized FTE/accuracy benefit)
Controls: - CTL-630 (ensure controlled execution — Process Mining, Process Analysis & Improvement Project Execution (PA-133.2).)
- CTL-630: build/buy/integrate decision via EA; TCO and benefit verified by Finance
Pain Points / Risks: - **Wrong-tool risk**: RPA where integration is better (brittle, costly); mitigated by EA review (VS-113) and "buy/integrate-first" principle
- **Benefit-overstate risk**: Automation that mimics a broken process; mitigated by re-design first (W4060)
System Touchpoints: - Process mining (W4058); RPA/automation platform (links to VS-30.2); EA/integration (links to VS-113); TBM/TCO (links to VS-135)

steps.activity: OpEx scope the automation opportunity: the manual steps, volume/effort, variability, systems/data involved, and the candidate technology (RPA, IDP/OCR, workflow, API integration)
OpEx/Finance build the business case (effort saved, accuracy/revenue benefit, TCO links to VS-135, sustainability), and route build vs buy to innovation/EA (VS-30/VS-113)
OpEx hand off approved automations to the build pipeline (VS-30.2 RPA lifecycle / VS-113 integration), and track realized benefit (W4065)

fields.Owner: OpEx Process Lead / Risk & Controls (links to VS-21)
fields.Participants: OpEx, Internal Audit (VS-21), Risk (VS-21.2), Compliance (VS-22), process owner
fields.Trigger: Re-designed process; audit finding; control failure

workflows.name: Control Design & Re-Engineering for Risk Reduction

Automation Opportunity: - System-enforced controls (workflow gates, segregation-of-duties); continuous control monitoring
Controls: - CTL-630: control design reviewed by Internal Audit; changes registered and tested
Cross-references: - links to VS-21 (audit), VS-21.2 (risk), VS-22 (compliance), internal-controls-matrix
Pain Points / Risks: - **Control-gap risk**: Re-design removes an existing control inadvertently; mitigated by control-mapping and audit validation
- **Over-control risk**: Controls that strangle efficiency; mitigated by risk-based design and continuous review
System Touchpoints: - Internal controls matrix; risk register (links to VS-21.2); SOP library (VS-30.3); monitoring dashboard (W4066)

steps.activity: OpEx design/re-engineer preventive and detective controls into the future-state process (system-enforced where possible), aligned to the internal-controls-matrix and risk register (VS-21.2)
OpEx/Audit validate the control design (does it mitigate the risk without excessive burden), and update the controls register (links to internal-controls-matrix)
OpEx embed the control into SOPs (W4060) and monitoring (W4066), and confirm post-rollout (W4092)

fields.Owner: OpEx Process Lead / OCM Lead (links to VS-134)
fields.Participants: OCM (VS-134), process owners, store/DC leadership, training (VS-19.4), comms (VS-103.1)
fields.Volume: Per improvement project (often network-wide: 200 stores / 4 DCs)

Automation Opportunity: - Rollout tracking across 200 sites; adoption-rate monitoring with site-level intervention triggers
Controls: - CTL-630 (ensure controlled execution — Process Mining, Process Analysis & Improvement Project Execution (PA-133.2).)
- CTL-630: sustainment owner assigned; control-stage sign-off; benefit verified at +90 days (W4065)
Cross-references: - links to VS-134 (OCM), VS-19.4 (training), W4066 (monitoring), W4065 (benefit)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Reversion risk**: Sites revert to old ways post-rollout; mitigated by sustainment controls and adoption monitoring (W4092)
- **Change-saturation risk**: Too many changes at once; mitigated by OCM portfolio/capacity view (VS-134)
System Touchpoints: - OCM platform (links to VS-134); training/LMS (VS-19.4); comms (VS-103.1); monitoring (W4066)
Time Estimate: - Weeks to months depending on scope (network rollout)

steps.activity: OpEx/OCM build the rollout plan (phasing across sites, training cascade, comms, hypercare) and engage OCM for the people side (links to VS-134)
OpEx/leadership execute the phased rollout, monitor adoption and KPIs, and intervene where adoption lags (links to W4091/W4092)
OpEx hand over to the process owner for sustainment, lock in controls (W4063) and standard work (W4060), and transition monitoring to the control tower (W4066)
